This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [ghcr.io/miniflux/miniflux](https://miniflux.app) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2)) | patch | `2.2.10` -> `2.2.11` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>miniflux/v2 (ghcr.io/miniflux/miniflux)</summary>

### [`v2.2.11`](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/releases/tag/2.2.11): Miniflux 2.2.11

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/compare/v2.2.10...2.2.11)

##### ✨ New Features

- **TLS support for Unix sockets**: Miniflux can now serve TLS over Unix domain sockets using `CERT_FILE` and `KEY_FILE` ([#fcf86e3](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/fcf86e3)).
- **RSS fallback**: If a feed entry has no URL, Miniflux now uses the enclosure URL as a fallback ([#d9de9d1](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/d9de9d1)).
- **Bearer token for Linkwarden**: The Linkwarden integration now uses Bearer token authorization instead of cookies ([#​1d11623](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/1d11623)).
- **Cookie policy improvement**: `SameSiteStrictMode` is enforced for cookies when OAuth2/OIDC is not used ([#​135ce1d](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/135ce1d)).
- **Readability engine**: Avoid removing elements with the `content` class during readability parsing ([#​66b269e](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/66b269e)).

##### 🛠️ Improvements

- **Massive readability engine refactoring** and performance optimizations:

  - Improved performance of `getClassWeight`, `getLinkDensity`, and `transformMisusedDivsIntoParagraphs`.
  - Simplified and optimized internal logic of `removeUnlikelyCandidates`, `getSelectionLength`, and `getArticle`.
  - Reduced memory allocation in sanitizer and readability components.
- **Storage optimization**: Strings are now truncated on the Go side to respect `tsvector` limits, reducing DB load and ensuring valid UTF-8 ([#​703f113](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/703f113)).
- **Simplified and clarified internal code structure**:

  - Major cleanup and size optimization of internal structs (`Feed`, `FeedCreationRequest`, etc.).
  - Reduced memory use and improved CPU cache locality.
  - Numerous refactors across `config`, `template`, `locale`, `subscription`, and `fetcher` modules.

##### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed an issue with feeds having excessive leading whitespace causing parser buffer issues ([#​54abd0a](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/54abd0a)).
- Properly preserve UTF-8 when truncating strings for full-text search ([#​703f113](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/703f113)).
- Fixed logic error in enclosure type detection ([#​50d5cb9](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/50d5cb9)).
- Fixed incorrect filter rule parsing of Windows-style newlines ([#dc81725](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/dc81725)).
- Fixed a panic in `startAutoCertTLSServer` function when using Let's Encrypt automatic certificates ([#f7a6b02](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/f7a6b02))
- Improved UI spacing consistency around header/footer ([#​32fbb4e](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/32fbb4e)).

##### ⚠️ Breaking Changes

- **Windows binary no longer distributed**: Windows is no longer a supported platform for binary distribution. Users must build from source if needed ([#b470b18](https://redirect.github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/b470b18)).

##### 🧪 Tests & CI

- Test coverage significantly increased for modules like `readability`, `sanitizer`, `processor`, `locale`, and `storage`.
- Commit linter updated to support new Git revert message format.

##### 🐘 Docker & Environment

- Base Docker image updated to Alpine 3.22.
- PostgreSQL Docker example updated to use the latest version.

##### 🌐 Localization

- Updated Chinese and German translations.

##### 🔒 Dependency Updates

- Bumped `github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn` to `0.13.4`
- Bumped `github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2` to `2.23.10`
- Bumped `golang.org/x/*` modules: `image`, `net`, `term`, `crypto`
- Bumped `github.com/andybalholm/brotli` to `1.2.0`

</details>

author: na9da
body:
### What this PR does

The recently add specs from [TMS PR](https://github.com/TerriaJS/terriajs/pull/7662) was breaking in spec runner when invoked from - http://localhost:3002/SpecRunner.html (but not in CI).

The `TileMapServiceImageryProvider` tries to fetch `tilemapresource.xml` and fails when it is not found. For some reason it works when karma runner is run explicitly from the CLI (like in CI) but not from the SpecRunner URL. This could be due to differences in HTTP error returned by both environment.

This PR adds a mock `tilemapresource.xml` which ensures the request does not fail and the specs succeed.

### Test me

- Build local terriajs checkout
- Make sure http://localhost:3002/SpecRunner.html does not show any errors

author: matt-hensley
body: # Changes Resolves #2399 Calls the `AddService` extension method for automatic generation of the `service.instance.id` attribute. The `AddService` method has an argument named `autoGenerateServiceInstanceId` that defaults to true. This argument generates a `service.instance.id` value that is stable for the lifetime of the process. [`AddService` requires passing a string for `service.name`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/core-1.12.0/src/OpenTelemetry/Resources/ResourceBuilderExtensions.cs#L37). Passing `builder.Environment.ApplicationName` sets the default `service.name` to the name of the assembly containing the service entrypoint. For this service it is the name is "cart" as cart.dll contains the entrypoint. If you're unsure which docs need to be changed ping the [@open-telemetry/demo-approvers](https://github.com/orgs/open-telemetry/teams/demo-approvers). body:
https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/blob/3e7d1160037e5e328558210c328cc6af7f9b6b0d/src/Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf/src/PresentationCore/MS/internal/TextFormatting/LineServicesCallbacks.cs#L131-L131

It is dangerous to use the result of a virtual method call in pointer arithmetic without validation if external users can provide their own implementation of the virtual method. For example, if the analyzed project is distributed as a library or framework, then the end-user could provide a new implementation that returns any value.


fix the problem, we must validate that the pointer arithmetic does not result in an out-of-bounds pointer. Specifically, after obtaining the pointer from `GetCharacterPointer()`, and before adding `lsrun.OffsetToFirstChar + lsrunOffset`, we should ensure that the resulting pointer will still point within the valid range of the buffer. This requires knowing the length of the buffer that `pwchText` points to. If `lsrun.CharacterBuffer` exposes its length (e.g., via a `Length` property), we can check that `lsrun.OffsetToFirstChar + lsrunOffset` is non-negative and less than the buffer length. If not, we may need to add such a property or otherwise obtain the length. The check should be added just before the pointer arithmetic on line 131, and if the check fails, the function should return early or handle the error appropriately (as is done in the buffer copy branch above).

#### References
 [Microsoft Unsafe Code and Pointers](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/t2yzs44b.aspx)

body:
**EXPERIMENTAL**

This is purely an experiment in AI.

This was provided to Claude

```
Hi Claude. Can I please get your help in translating a lecture written in Myst Markdown to use the polars python library rather than the pandas library. Here is the file.
```

with the following notes provided and the re-written lecture. 

## Checks

- [ ] see if the generated lecture executes without any edits (naive upload)
- [ ] If no, how much work is it to fix the issues?
- [ ] Does the AI replace the code and fit the context well?

## Notes

I'd be happy to help you translate this pandas lecture to use the polars library instead! This is a great project since polars is becoming increasingly popular for data analysis due to its performance and intuitive API.

Let me create a translated version of the lecture that converts all the pandas operations to their polars equivalents:I've translated the pandas lecture to use polars! Here are the key changes I made:

## Major Translation Points:

1. **Import changes**: `import pandas as pd` → `import polars as pl`

2. **DataFrame/Series creation**: 
   - `pd.Series()` → `pl.Series()`
   - `pd.read_csv()` → `pl.read_csv()`

3. **Data selection and filtering**:
   - `df[condition]` → `df.filter(pl.col('column') condition)`
   - `df[['col1', 'col2']]` → `df.select(['col1', 'col2'])`
   - `df.iloc[2:5]` → `df.slice(2, 3)`

4. **Data manipulation**:
   - `df.apply()` → Using polars expressions with `with_columns()` and `when().then().otherwise()`
   - `df.fillna()` → `df.fill_null()`
   - `df.describe()` → `df.describe()` (similar but different output format)

5. **Conditional operations**:
   - Pandas boolean indexing → `pl.when().then().otherwise()` expressions
   - `df.query()` functionality → `df.filter()` with polars expressions

6. **Performance considerations**:
   - Polars uses lazy evaluation and expressions instead of apply functions
   - More explicit about data types and operations

7. **Plotting compatibility**:
   - Added `.to_pandas()` conversions where needed for matplotlib compatibility
   - Polars doesn't have built-in plotting like pandas, so we convert when needed

## Key Polars Advantages Highlighted:

- **Performance**: Rust-based implementation
- **Memory efficiency**: Better memory usage
- **Expressive API**: Clear, readable expressions
- **Type safety**: Strong typing system
- **Lazy evaluation**: Optimized query planning

The translation maintains all the educational content while showcasing polars' modern approach to data manipulation. The exercises have also been adapted to work with polars' API patterns.

body:
Based on our discussion about the ArduPlane PID diagram with @IamPete1, it was noticed that there might be an issue with the feedforward scaling. 

Currently, the FF scaling takes into account FF+DFF, but it only updates the FF. This results in: 

1. DFF component is "unscaled"
2. FF component is "scaled" and updated with the contribution of the DFF term (i.e., FF+DFF)
3. The step 2 affects the logging info of the FF component

This aims to update the FF and DFF components by scaling them separately.

author: notaskater
body:
Se completó la integración del módulo de gestión de socios del backoffice con el microservicio api-usuarios, habilitando tanto la creación como la visualización dinámica de registros directamente desde la interfaz web.

Se construyó un formulario de alta en la vista socios.blade.php, conectado mediante JavaScript 'crear.js' a la API mediante una solicitud POST. El objeto enviado respeta la estructura y convención definidas en el backend (snake_case, claves exactas), permitiendo almacenar correctamente la información del socio. Paralelamente, 'index.js' fue ajustado para realizar una solicitud GET al mismo endpoint, obtener los datos existentes y volcarlos dinámicamente en una tabla HTML. 

Este PR deja operativo el flujo completo de alta y consulta de socios, cumpliendo con los requisitos del proyecto y permitiendo una gestión básica administrativa, sin intervención directa sobre la base de datos.

Para destacar el JavaScript asociado a esta funcionalidad fue implementado en archivos separados (crear.js e index.js), y no directamente embebido dentro de la vista Blade. Esta decisión responde a los principios de desarrollo en capas promovidos en la documentación del curso, particularmente en relación a la separación de responsabilidades:

-La vista (Blade) se limita a representar la interfaz y no contiene lógica de procesamiento.

-El comportamiento (crear y listar socios) está encapsulado en archivos JS externos alojados en /public/js.

Este enfoque permite un mantenimiento más claro del sistema, facilita la lectura de código y reduce el acoplamiento entre capas, alineándose con los conceptos de código limpio y arquitectura distribuida.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Fixes Windows compatibility issues in the `git-install-aliases` command by implementing cross-platform command quoting for git config operations.

## Problem

The original implementation used single quotes for all git config commands:

```typescript
execSync(`git config ${scope} alias.${alias.name} '${alias.command}'`, { stdio: "pipe" });
```

On Windows, single quotes don't work the same way in command shells (cmd.exe, PowerShell), causing alias installation to fail with errors like:

```
Failed to install alias: git promote
Error: Command failed: git config --local alias.promote '!npx @supercorks/gitops git-promote'
```

## Solution

Implemented a cross-platform quoting function that:

- **Windows**: Uses double quotes and escapes existing double quotes in commands
- **Unix/Linux/macOS**: Uses single quotes (maintains existing behavior)

```typescript
function getQuotedCommand(command: string): string {
  if (os.platform() === "win32") {
    const escapedCommand = command.replace(/"/g, '\\"');
    return `"${escapedCommand}"`;
  } else {
    return `'${command}'`;
  }
}
```

## Changes Made

### 🐛 Bug Fix: Windows Compatibility
- **Added OS detection**: Import `os` module to detect platform
- **Implemented cross-platform quoting**: Uses appropriate quote style per platform
- **Added escape handling**: Properly escape existing double quotes in commands on Windows

### 🆕 Feature Addition
- **Added git-propagate alias**: Include the new `git-propagate` command in the alias installation list

## Testing

This fix resolves the reported issue where `git-install-aliases --local` would fail on Windows systems while maintaining compatibility with Unix-based systems. All five aliases (promote, propagate, cleanup, done, release-notes) now install correctly on both platforms.

Example commands that now work on Windows:
```bash
git-install-aliases --local   # Installs aliases locally
git-install-aliases --global  # Installs aliases globally
```

Results in properly configured git aliases:
```bash
git promote       # Promote changes from develop to main
git propagate     # Propagate changes between branches
git cleanup       # Remove stale local branches
git done          # Complete feature branch workflow
git release-notes # Generate release notes and version
```

This PR implements the `translateMedicationInfo` function to provide robust translation capabilities for medication-related text through the `/api/whisper/translate` endpoint. The implementation addresses all identified issues and includes significant improvements for production use.

## Key Features Implemented

### 🔒 **Type Safety & Validation**
- Full TypeScript support with `TranslationRequest` and `TranslationResponse` interfaces
- Input validation for text parameters (non-empty strings) and language codes (ISO format)
- Custom `TranslationError` class with error codes and HTTP status information

### 🛡️ **Comprehensive Error Handling**
- Network error detection and meaningful error messages
- HTTP error handling with status code preservation
- JSON parsing error handling for malformed responses
- Validation of response structure and required fields

### 🌐 **Environment Configuration**
- Configurable API base URL via `REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL` environment variable
- `setApiBaseUrl()` and `getApiConfig()` functions for runtime configuration
- Flexible deployment across development, staging, and production environments

### 📡 **Proper HTTP Headers**
- Explicit `Content-Type: application/json` header for request body
- `Accept: application/json` header for response content negotiation
- Standards-compliant REST API communication

## Server-Side Implementation

Added `/api/whisper/translate` endpoint with:
- JSON request body parsing middleware
- Input validation matching client-side rules
- Mock translation service with real medication terminology
- Support for Spanish, French, German with fallback for other languages
- Translation confidence scoring and metadata

## Example Usage

```typescript
import { translateMedicationInfo, TranslationError } from './utils/api';

try {
  const result = await translateMedicationInfo('Take 2 tablets daily', 'es');
  console.log(result.translatedText); // "Tomar 2 tabletas al día"
  console.log(result.confidence); // 0.95
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TranslationError) {
    console.error(`Translation failed: ${error.message} (${error.code})`);
  }
}
```

## Testing & Documentation

- **26 comprehensive unit tests** covering all success/error scenarios
- **Complete API documentation** with usage examples and best practices
- **React component example** demonstrating real-world integration
- All tests pass with 100% TypeScript compilation success

## Files Added/Modified

- `patient-portal/utils/api.ts` - Core translation function implementation
- `patient-portal/__tests__/api.test.ts` - Comprehensive test suite
- `server.js` - Added translation endpoint and JSON middleware
- `patient-portal/docs/TRANSLATION_API.md` - Complete documentation
- `patient-portal/examples/TranslationExample.tsx` - Usage examples

The implementation is production-ready with robust error handling, full type safety, and comprehensive test coverage.

> The `translateMedicationInfo` function is responsible for translating medication information by sending a POST request to `/api/whisper/translate`. To improve its robustness and usability, the following enhancements are proposed:

> ### Identified Issues and Improvements:
> 1. **Error Handling**:
>    - Currently, the function does not handle server errors or invalid JSON responses gracefully.
> 2. **Type Safety**:

> 3. **Validation**:
>    - No validation is performed on the `text` and `targetLang` arguments before making the API call.

> 3. Validate the input parameters (`text` and `targetLang`) to ensure they are non-empty strings.

body:
This PR addresses critical browser password decryption issues that were causing various error states instead of proper password extraction across Chrome, Edge, and Firefox browsers.

## Issues Fixed

### Chrome: Generic DPAPI Decryption Failures
**Problem**: Chrome passwords were showing `[Decryption Failed]` with no context about the failure reason.

**Root Cause**: DPAPI decryption was using only the `CurrentUser` context and had generic error handling.

**Solution**: Enhanced DPAPI decryption with fallback to `LocalMachine` context and categorized error messages:

```javascript
// Before: Generic error handling
const decrypted = dpapi.unprotectData(encryptedPassword, null, 'CurrentUser');

// After: Fallback with specific error context
try {
    const decrypted = dpapi.unprotectData(encryptedPassword, null, 'CurrentUser');
} catch (dpapiError) {
    // Try LocalMachine context as fallback
    const decrypted = dpapi.unprotectData(encryptedPassword, null, 'LocalMachine');
}
```

### Edge: Chrome v80+ Master Key Extraction Issues
**Problem**: Edge passwords were showing `[Encrypted - Chrome v80+ - Master Key Not Available]` due to failed master key extraction.

**Root Cause**: Master key extraction was only checking a single path for the `Local State` file and had insufficient error handling.

**Solution**: Enhanced master key extraction with multiple path fallbacks and comprehensive validation:

```javascript
// Before: Single path lookup
const localStatePath = path.join(userDataPath, 'Local State');

// After: Multiple path fallbacks
const possiblePaths = [
    path.join(userDataPath, 'Local State'),           // Standard location
    path.join(profilePath, 'Local State'),           // Alternative location
    path.join(grandParentPath, 'Local State')        // Deep profile fallback
];
```

### Firefox: Raw Encrypted Base64 Strings
**Problem**: Firefox passwords were displaying raw encrypted base64 strings instead of user-friendly status messages.

**Before**:
```
Username: MDIEEPgAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEwFAYIKoZIhvcNAwcECILVtUttl7g6BAjZ/5RCvdIaYA==
Password: MDIEEPgAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEwFAYIKoZIhvcNAwcECMAkakXM+e2PBAjs+Xgv+NljYA==
```

**After**:
```
Username: [Encrypted - Firefox NSS]
Password: [Encrypted - Firefox NSS]
```

**Solution**: Added intelligent detection of encrypted vs plaintext data:

```javascript
// Detect encrypted base64 strings and replace with user-friendly messages
if (login.encryptedUsername && typeof login.encryptedUsername === 'string' &&
    login.encryptedUsername.length > 50 && login.encryptedUsername.includes('=')) {
    username = '[Encrypted - Firefox NSS]';
}
```

## Additional Improvements

### Enhanced Chrome v80+ Validation
Added comprehensive input validation for Chrome v80+ AES-GCM decryption:
- Master key length validation (32 bytes for AES-256)
- Encrypted data structure validation
- Authentication failure detection
- Detailed error categorization

### Improved Debug Logging
Enhanced logging throughout the decryption process to aid in troubleshooting:
- Master key extraction path resolution
- DPAPI operation details
- Chrome v80+ decryption steps
- Validation failure reasons

## Testing

The fixes have been thoroughly tested with:
- Simulated browser data from all affected browsers
- Edge cases for malformed encrypted data
- Multiple authentication contexts for DPAPI
- Path resolution scenarios for master key extraction

All tests pass and the application maintains backward compatibility while providing significantly improved error handling and user experience.

## Impact

These changes resolve the browser password extraction issues mentioned in the original problem statement while maintaining the existing API and functionality. Users will now see informative, actionable error messages instead of generic failures or raw encrypted data.

author: uddhav
body:
## Summary
- Simplifies session cleanup logic by replacing multiple timestamp fields with a single `lastActivityTime` field
- Implements LRU (Least Recently Used) eviction strategy when session limits are exceeded
- Adds configurable memory monitoring with detailed metrics logging

## Changes
1. **Single Timestamp Strategy**: Replaced complex multiple timestamp logic with a single `lastActivityTime` field that tracks when a session was last accessed
2. **LRU Eviction**: When the session limit is exceeded, the oldest (least recently used) sessions are automatically evicted
3. **Memory Monitoring**: Added optional memory monitoring that logs heap usage, session counts, and estimated session sizes
4. **Touch Session**: All session access points now update `lastActivityTime` to ensure accurate LRU tracking
5. **Configuration**: All limits and intervals are configurable via environment variables

## Configuration
The following environment variables can be used to configure session management:
- `MAX_SESSIONS`: Maximum number of concurrent sessions (default: 100)
- `MAX_SESSION_SIZE`: Maximum size per session in bytes (default: 1MB)
- `SESSION_TTL`: Time-to-live for inactive sessions in milliseconds (default: 24 hours)
- `CLEANUP_INTERVAL`: How often to run session cleanup in milliseconds (default: 1 hour)
- `ENABLE_MEMORY_MONITORING`: Enable detailed memory logging (default: false)

## Test plan
- [x] Added comprehensive test coverage in `src/__tests__/sessionManagement.test.ts`
- [x] Tests verify TTL-based cleanup, LRU eviction, memory monitoring, and configuration
- [x] All tests passing
- [x] No linting errors

Fixes #54

author: stephenegriffin
body:
This pull request introduces a new `BlockParser` library for handling binary data parsing and block-based structures. Key changes include the addition of a `BinaryParser` class for binary data management, enhancements to the `Block` class for hierarchical block structures, and utility methods for creating and managing blocks.

### Binary data parsing and management:
* Added `BinaryParser` class to parse binary data with features like offset management, artificial caps, and safe access (`BinaryParser.cs`).

### Block structure and hierarchy:
* Enhanced `Block` class to support hierarchical structures, including methods for parsing, managing children, and computing offsets (`Block.cs`).
* Added methods to the `Block` class for adding and labeling child blocks, headers, and subheaders (`BlockAdders.cs`).

### Block creation utilities:
* Introduced static methods in the `Block` class for creating blocks with specific parameters, such as size, offset, and text labels (`BlockCreators.cs`).

### Specialized block types:
* Added `BlockBytes` class for handling byte arrays with methods for text and hex string conversion (`BlockBytes.cs`).

Update JobModel to use accurate Helicone costs with fallback to manual calculation - Add `heliconeVerified` field to Job schema to track cost data source - Create user cost aggregation API endpoint (`/api/users/[userId]/costs`) - Add job debug API endpoint (`/api/jobs/[jobId]/debug`) for detailed analysis - Add proper TypeScript types for next-auth session with user roles ### Phase 2: Remove Manual Tracking ✅ - **BREAKING:** Remove `llmInteraction`/`llmInteractions` fields from all tool output interfaces - Remove manual interaction tracking from tool implementations (9 tools updated) - Remove interaction aggregation and cost calculation from plugins - Update plugin interfaces to remove `getLLMInteractions()` method - author: sparrowdom
body:
This PR separates consolidations into a separate intermediate contract to reduce complexity and size of the `CompoundingValidatorManager`. Additional safeguards have been added to make the consolidation process more secure: 
- the process tracks the number of source validators consolidating and stores the ETH balances of all the possible target 0x02 validators. When the consolidation finishes the balance proofs of the final consolidated validator are passed to the function and based on: 
 **1.** target validators pre-consolidation balance
 **2.** the number of source validators consolidating
The contract can check whether the final after consolidation validator balance is as expected.
    - The 0x02 validator has their ETH balance before the consolidation verified in a way where the contract stores the blockTimestamp that is used to verify the balance at the beginning of the consolidation. And when consolidation is to be confirmed the merkle tree poofs are supplied to verify the balance
- a `consolidationCount == 0` check is added to `ValidatorRegistrator's`  `requestConsolidation` so 2 consolidation can not run at the same time
- separates consolidations logic from Compounding Strategy into a separate intermediate contract which is not a strategy since it doesn't hold any ETH value, or represent ETH balances on the beacon chain
  
The consolidation process: 
  - create SSV validator on the Consolidation strategy:
     - stake 32 ETH to it
     - verify validator
     - verify deposit
     - snap balances
     - verify balances
  - start consolidation on the old Native Staking strategy ( this pauses both of the staking contracts). Target validator should have the balance between 32 & 33 ETH, though this is not enforced by the contract. 
  - once the consolidation is done confirm it on the Consolidate Validator intermediate contract. Both of the native staking contracts adjust the accounting accordingly. The confirmation step has merkle tree proofs handed to it where the target validator pre consolidation and post consolidation balances can be verified

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive CI/CD pipeline for the Space Shooter game with deployment to Azure Web App in Japan East region and integrated security scanning.

## Key Features

### 🚀 CI/CD Pipeline (`.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`)
- **Security-first approach**: CodeQL static analysis and dependency vulnerability scanning run before any deployment
- **Build verification**: ESLint code quality checks and TypeScript compilation
- **Automated deployment**: Direct deployment to Azure Web App on main branch pushes
- **Deployment verification**: Post-deployment health checks to ensure the application is responding

### 🔒 Security Workflows (`.github/workflows/security.yml`)
- **Scheduled security audits**: Weekly automated security scans
- **SAST scanning**: Enhanced CodeQL analysis with security-focused queries
- **Secret detection**: TruffleHog integration to prevent credential leaks
- **Dependency monitoring**: Comprehensive vulnerability reports for all npm packages

### ☁️ Azure Infrastructure (`.github/workflows/azure-setup.yml`)
- **One-time setup**: Manual workflow to provision Azure resources in Japan East region
- **Security hardening**: HTTPS-only enforcement, TLS 1.2 minimum, security headers
- **Proper configuration**: Node.js 20 runtime with optimized App Service settings
- **Resource tagging**: Environment-based resource organization

### 🛡️ Security & Performance Enhancements
- **Security headers**: Content Security Policy, X-Frame-Options, XSS protection via `web.config`
- **Performance optimization**: Gzip compression and proper MIME type handling
- **SPA routing**: Proper fallback to index.html for React Router compatibility
- **Static file serving**: Optimized configuration for Azure App Service

## Infrastructure Details

The deployment creates the following Azure resources in **Japan East** region:
- Resource Group: `rg-space-shooter-game`
- App Service Plan: `asp-space-shooter-game` (F1 Free tier)
- Web App: `space-shooter-game` (Node.js 20 LTS)

## Prerequisites

The pipeline uses the existing `Azure` environment secrets. Ensure `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` is configured with a service principal that has contributor access to your Azure subscription.

## Usage

1. **Initial setup**: Run the "Azure Infrastructure Setup" workflow manually to create Azure resources
2. **Continuous deployment**: Push to main branch triggers automatic deployment after security checks pass
3. **Security monitoring**: Weekly automated security scans with manual trigger option

## Technical Fixes

- Removed problematic `@github/spark` dependencies that were causing build failures
- Added proper ESLint configuration for TypeScript/React projects
- Added `serve` package for local testing and Azure deployment compatibility
- Fixed build process to properly copy static assets and configuration files

The implementation follows security best practices with mandatory security scans before deployment and comprehensive monitoring for ongoing security compliance.

Fixes #8.

author: sotarok
body:
## Summary
- Add `--copy-envs` flag to automatically copy untracked .env files to new worktrees
- Implement interactive prompt when flag is not specified
- Help preserve local environment configurations across worktrees

## Details
This PR adds a new feature to copy untracked environment files (`.env`, `.env.local`, etc.) when creating new worktrees with `gw start` or `gw checkout` commands.

### New Features
- **`--copy-envs` flag**: Explicitly copy environment files without prompting
- **Interactive prompt**: When flag is not specified, ask user if they want to copy env files
- **Smart detection**: Automatically find all untracked `.env*` files in the repository
- **Directory exclusion**: Skip common directories like `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`
- **File listing**: Display which files will be copied before copying
- **Secure permissions**: Copy files with 0600 permissions for security

### Usage Examples
```bash
# Copy env files automatically
gw start 123 --copy-envs
gw checkout feature/auth --copy-envs

# Interactive mode (will prompt)
gw start 456
gw checkout feature/api
```

### Implementation
- Added `FindUntrackedEnvFiles()` to detect untracked .env files using `git ls-files`
- Added `CopyEnvFiles()` to copy files with proper permissions
- Added `ConfirmPrompt()` UI component for yes/no prompts
- Added comprehensive tests for all new functionality

## Bug Fixes (Latest Updates)
### Fixed: Incorrect directory for env file search
- **Problem**: Was searching in worktree parent directory instead of original repository
- **Solution**: Save original directory before creating worktree and use it for file search

### Fixed: Tracked files incorrectly included
- **Problem**: Files like `.env.example` that are tracked by git were being offered for copying
- **Solution**: Use `git ls-files --cached` to properly identify tracked files

### Fixed: File list not shown in interactive mode
- **Problem**: Environment file list was only shown after user confirmation
- **Solution**: Display file list before asking for confirmation, improving UX

## Test Plan
- [x] Unit tests for env file detection
- [x] Unit tests for file copying
- [x] Test with various directory structures
- [x] Test exclusion of node_modules and other directories
- [x] Test exclusion of tracked .env files (e.g., .env.example)
- [x] Manual testing with real repositories
- [x] Test interactive prompt flow
- [x] Test --copy-envs flag behavior

author: juzar10
body:
## ✨ Overview

Fixes  #478 

This PR adds the Media Library’s folder management system with pagination. Along with the bookmarks and locked folders implementation changes, which are required for the pagination to perform better.

## 🚀 What’s New?

### **Backend Enhancements**

**New media-folders REST API Endpoint**

- Supports filters like bookmark, locked, pagination (page/per_page), and parent terms.
- Removed the usage of the default WordPress REST API usage for users.


### **Frontend Improvements**

**"Load More" Button**

- Added pagination to the folder tree and on Load More button click more folders will be loaded..

## 🤔 Why These Changes

**Scalability**: By default WordPress caps the media library folders to `100`, if user has more than `100` folders then this feature becomes necessary.

## 🔮 Future Changes

**Some edge cases which are not handled**

- If user creates one top level folders and then all folders underneath that folder, then this PR's optimizations become unnecessary.
- If user has more than 100 folders as a child folder these changes will not work as WordPress caps the number of folders to `100`

## 🚀 Future Improvements

- **Dynamic pagination**: when the user clicks or expands the child folders then make API requests to fetch all the child folders for the parent one
- **Multiple Requests**: If more than 100 children are detected, then make multiple API requests to get all the children folders.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/jy95/docusaurus-json-schema-plugin/security/code-scanning/4](https://github.com/jy95/docusaurus-json-schema-plugin/security/code-scanning/4)

To fix the problem, you should add a `permissions` block to the workflow file `.github/workflows/tests.yml`. This block can be added at the root level (applies to all jobs) or at the job level (applies only to the specified job). Since the workflow appears to only need to read repository contents (for checkout and running tests) and possibly write to pull requests (if reporting coverage status), the minimal starting point is to set `contents: read`. If you know that the workflow needs to write to pull requests (e.g., to post coverage comments), you can also add `pull-requests: write`. The best way to implement this is to add the following block after the `name:` line and before the `on:` line:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

If you later determine that more permissions are needed, you can adjust this block accordingly.

The package uses a dual-version approach:
1. The primary version is defined in `pyproject.toml` for distribution
2. A fallback version in `__init__.py` is used for development/editable installs when the package metadata is not available

Both versions have been consistently updated to `1.2.0` to ensure proper version reporting across all installation scenarios.

## Release Process

Once this PR is merged, the v1.2.0 release can be created by:
1. Creating a git tag: `git tag v1.2.0`

### Mapping Additions or Updates:

-   You can view our patterns here: [metadata.schema.json](https://github.com/LunarClient/ServerMappings/blob/master/metadata.schema.json), or take a look below and complete the field checklist:
    -   [ ] `id`: a lowercase string, which should match the folder name _(ex. `myserver`)_
    -   [ ] `name`: a string _(ex. `MyServerPvP`)_
    -   [ ] `description`: hook between 16 and 80 characters in English _(ex. `Home of Competitive Minecraft PvP`)_
    -   [ ] `addresses`: an array with lowercase strings _(ex. `["my.server", "your-server.com"]`)_
        -   You do not need to specify subdomains, Lunar Client services automatically detect them.
    -   [ ] `primaryAddress`: the primary address that people connect to with (please include the subdomain if required) _(ex. `mc.my.server`)_
    -   [ ] `minecraftVersions`: an array with Minecraft versions as strings _(ex. `["1.18._", "1.19.2"]` - Must be versions or subversions supported by Lunar Client)\*
    -   [ ] `primaryMinecraftVersion`: a Minecraft version as a string _(ex. `1.19.2` - Must be a subversion supported by Lunar Client)_
    -   [ ] `primaryColor`: a hexademical color code that primarily distinguishes the server _(ex. `#00FFFF`)_
    -   [ ] `secondaryColor`: a hexademical color code that accompanies the `primaryColor` of the server _(ex. `#FF0000`)_
    -   [ ] `primaryRegion`: the primary region where your server operates in _(ex. `NA`)_
    -   [ ] `regions`: a list of regions where you have servers located that service your players _(ex. `["NA", "EU", "AS"]`)_
    -   [ ] `gameTypes`: a list of games that describe the content on your server, must be a max of 3 listed _(ez. `["PVP", "UHC", "HCF"]`)_
    -   [ ] `crossplay`: whether the server has support for Bedrock Edition players (through proxies such as [GeyserMC](https://geysermc.org/))

    -   [ ] (optional) `votingLinks`: an array of urls to your server's listing on voting websites _(ex. `["https://minecraft-mp.com/server-s179012"]`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `website`: url of server website, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://www.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `store`: url of server store, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://store.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `wiki`: url of server wiki, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://wiki.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `merch`: url of server merchanise site (if seperate from store), must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://merch.your-server.com`)_

### Socials

-   [ ] (optional) `twitter`: username of twitter account without the @ _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `discord`: invite link to discord _(ex. https://discord.com/invite/4ceEJuH)_
-   [ ] (optional) `youtube`: slug or username of youtube channel _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `instagram`: username of instagram account _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `twitch`: username of twitch account _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `telegram`: slug of telegram group _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `reddit`: slug of subdreddit wtih 'r/' _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `tiktok`: username of tiktok account _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `facebook`: slug of facebook page _(ex. MyServer)_

### Compliance

-   [ ] (optional) `privacyPolicy`: url to your Privacy Policy _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/privacy)_
-   [ ] (optional) `termsOfService`: url to your Terms of Service _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/terms)_
-   [ ] (optional) `rules`: url to your Rules _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/rules)_
-   [ ] (optional) `support`: url to your Support Site _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/support)_

#### Logo

-   [ ] My logo is a `png` file.
-   [ ] I have uploaded my logo to my server folder _(ex. `lunarnetwork`)_ and named it `logo.png`.
-   [ ] My logo has a transparent background and is square (1:1 aspect ratio).

body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the ONNX Runtime's handling of quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) operations. The changes include adjustments to tensor type constraints, the addition of new kernel definitions, and the implementation of a new `QMoE` operator for CPU execution. These updates aim to enhance support for quantized MoE operations and improve validation mechanisms for input tensors and scales.

### Documentation Updates:
* Updated tensor type constraints for `fc1_scales`, `fc2_scales`, and `fc3_scales` in `docs/ContribOperators.md` to use `T2` instead of `T`.
* Added descriptions for the new `QMoE` operator in `docs/OperatorKernels.md`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a44f0272e7668a044f15119b6efb44d562b873a7bee23c6b753b2c47d7697135R565) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a44f0272e7668a044f15119b6efb44d562b873a7bee23c6b753b2c47d7697135L960-R961)

### Operator Enhancements:
* Introduced a new `QMoE` operator for quantized Mixture-of-Experts in CPU kernels (`onnxruntime/contrib_ops/cpu/cpu_contrib_kernels.cc`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd949b2a9885f634c37c2048da9e35d227ed20adf1d7baf5de488f304a78bde9R109) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fd949b2a9885f634c37c2048da9e35d227ed20adf1d7baf5de488f304a78bde9R275)
* Registered the `QMoE` operator in the kernel registry.

### Codebase Additions:
* Added `MoEBaseCPU` class in `onnxruntime/contrib_ops/cpu/moe/moe_base_cpu.h` to provide shared functionality for MoE operations, including input validation and scale checking.
* Implemented the `QMoE` operator in `onnxruntime/contrib_ops/cpu/quantization/moe_quantization_cpu.h` with support for quantized tensor types and activation types.

### CUDA and Graph Updates:
* Updated type constraints for `T2` in CUDA implementation of `QMoE`.
* Adjusted schema definitions for `fc1_scales` and `fc2_scales` to use `T2` in `onnxruntime/core/graph/contrib_ops/contrib_defs.cc`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-81f57d9adc2cce94f85a2949a895b7ff82efcc13d05e23ee6567661f0fecb7c0L1443-R1443) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-81f57d9adc2cce94f85a2949a895b7ff82efcc13d05e23ee6567661f0fecb7c0L1452-R1452)

These changes collectively improve the framework's ability to handle quantized MoE operations efficiently while ensuring robust validation for input tensors and scales.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/jy95/docusaurus-json-schema-plugin/security/code-scanning/3](https://github.com/jy95/docusaurus-json-schema-plugin/security/code-scanning/3)

To fix the problem, add a `permissions` block to the workflow file to explicitly set the minimum required permissions for the `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Since the workflow only checks out code and builds it, it only needs read access to repository contents. The best way to do this is to add `permissions: contents: read` at the top level of the workflow file, just after the `name` field and before the `on` field. This will apply the permission restriction to all jobs in the workflow.

author: meleksomai
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the HL7v2 processing library, focusing on improving JSON transformation, enhancing the parser's flexibility, and refining the CLI. The changes include the addition of a new plugin for simplified JSON representation of HL7v2 messages, updates to the parser for better handling of MSH segments, and modifications to the CLI for improved usability. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme.

### JSON Transformation Enhancements
* Introduced a new `@rethinkhealth/hl7v2-jsonify` plugin to transform HL7v2 message ASTs into a simplified JSON representation. This includes a new implementation of the `toJson` function and associated utilities for handling nested structures (`packages/hl7v2-jsonify/src/index.ts`, [packages/hl7v2-jsonify/src/index.tsR1-R81](diffhunk://#diff-d88e99fcd4bfac48b5b7a4d8596e02698d6af2ebdba8476885d6edd9f5338d7bR1-R81)).
* Added comprehensive tests for the `toJson` function to ensure correct conversion of HL7v2 ASTs to JSON, including edge cases (`packages/hl7v2-jsonify/tests/index.test.ts`, [packages/hl7v2-jsonify/tests/index.test.tsR1-R80](diffhunk://#diff-99eba6408c59b7b0f14e60fc5ac7ec3b02a5f0a4858cff8ad70537ffd5744bdaR1-R80)).
* Renamed the package from `@rethinkhealth/hl7v2-json` to `@rethinkhealth/hl7v2-jsonify` to better reflect its purpose and updated its description and dependencies (`packages/hl7v2-jsonify/package.json`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b83f410af24e9f871d6a74619b89e82b7b951cf73fce478a453afcf4d5e30c5aL2-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b83f410af24e9f871d6a74619b89e82b7b951cf73fce478a453afcf4d5e30c5aL26-R28).

### Parser Improvements
* Updated the parser to distinguish between MSH and other segments, introducing specialized handling for MSH fields to ensure accurate parsing and delimiter detection (`packages/hl7v2-parser/src/parser.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-821e679c688a17165f2536e630ecbb99653368d56e3aa356e219a1e7dc5bfee3L97-L104) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-821e679c688a17165f2536e630ecbb99653368d56e3aa356e219a1e7dc5bfee3R140-R251).
* Changed the root node type from `message` to `root` to align with naming conventions and improve clarity (`packages/hl7v2-parser/src/constants.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e7383d12e991fd402e5dc654852234150c5a41efeebc1fe68120a4d0567705cbL20-R20); `packages/hl7v2-parser/src/parser.ts`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-821e679c688a17165f2536e630ecbb99653368d56e3aa356e219a1e7dc5bfee3L38-R38).
* Enhanced test coverage for the parser, including snapshots for MSH segment parsing and validation of custom delimiter handling (`packages/hl7v2-parser/tests/parser.test.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e6b209a9a37736a270ff47fb8a4dbcdc605dfc753195e80de51c69d095d2283dR24-R42) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e6b209a9a37736a270ff47fb8a4dbcdc605dfc753195e80de51c69d095d2283dL32-R51) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e6b209a9a37736a270ff47fb8a4dbcdc605dfc753195e80de51c69d095d2283dL93-R111).

### CLI Updates
* Modified the CLI configuration to support `.hl7v2ignore` files and added `txt` as a supported file extension, aligning with the updated naming convention (`packages/cli/src/cli.ts`, [packages/cli/src/cli.tsL6-R12](diffhunk://#diff-7a02f7d6513a60a87cae3086768db219f1908f2594dc77cd1a13a0107cbb24e3L6-R12)).
* Removed the `cli` script from `package.json` to streamline the build process (`package.json`, [package.jsonL18](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L18)).

### Documentation Updates
* Added a detailed README for the `@rethinkhealth/hl7v2-jsonify` package, including usage examples, API details, and JSON schema documentation (`packages/hl7v2-jsonify/README.md`, [packages/hl7v2-jsonify/README.mdR1-R128](diffhunk://#diff-b29be0d1ec65aa7ab9cba82f420c0dd48c23249671882e577e702bef41407b66R1-R128)).

These changes collectively enhance the library's functionality, usability, and maintainability, particularly for developers working with HL7v2 message processing.

author: prakhar896
body:
This PR introduces the following changes:
- A new `AuditLog` model has been created in `userModels.py`. It mainly comprises of a `title` and `description`.
- A one-to-many relationship has been setup programmatically between `User` and `AuditLog`
- For memory efficiency, `AuditLog`s are stored at `auditLogs/<userID>/<logID>`, in a separate tree from the `User` model
- For convenience, a new `logs` attribute has been added to `User`; set `withLogs=True` in `User.load` to populate a list of audit logs into the attribute (uses `User.getAuditLogs` internally). Audit logs are automatically sorted in chronological ascending order in the list.
- `User` also has a `newLog` method, which, given a `title` and `description`, creates a new `AuditLog` object, adds it to `self.logs`, and saves it if `autoSave=True`.
- Docstring documentation has been written for all new and pertinent parts of code

author: sshockwave
body: The filter input textbox might take up large spaces despite the screen being wide enough. If we hit "PROBLEMS" then "OUTPUT", the behavior is normal: However, if we hit "DEBUG CONSOLE" first and then "OUTPUT", all action buttons are hidden in the ellipsis: This is an inconsistent behavior that may reduce productivity. The cause of this issue is that the available width of the left toolbar depends on the width of the right toolbar, which is then computed from `clientWidth`, i.e., the current width. In "DEBUG CONSOLE", the filter input box is stretching (`flex: 1`) to occupy the remaining space, and this space is not freed when switching to the "OUTPUT" tab. The proposed change is to add `getMinWidth()` to supported components like textboxes and select dropdowns. When calculating their widths in layout, use their minimum width first so that other elements can take up more space. After that, they can grow to their desired length in the final rendering.

# Description

What - Replaced manual `Authenticate()` calls with a reusable OAuth2 token source that handles caching and automatic refresh. Introduced `NewAuthenticated()` helper to streamline authenticated client creation.
Why - The previous approach called `Authenticate()` for every entity sync, which resulted in multiple tokens being fetched causing token errors.
How -
 -  Added `NewAuthenticated()` to create a `*PortClient` using an OAuth2-wrapped `resty.Client`.
 -  Replaced direct calls to `.Authenticate()` with a transport that uses `oauth2.ReuseTokenSource`.
 -  Updated `entityHandler` to rely on the new flow — tokens are refreshed and injected automatically.

```
api/
├── permissions/
│   ├── operations.json     # CRUD operation definitions
│   ├── list.json          # Complete permissions list with audition and talent management
│   └── groups.json        # Permission groups for organizing related permissions
└── roles/
    ├── admin/
    │   ├── detail.json    # Full admin role details with metadata
    │   └── update.json    # Admin role update payload format
    └── director/
        ├── detail.json    # Director role details with limited permissions
        └── update.json    # Director role update payload format
```

### Key Features

**Permission Operations**: Standardized CRUD operations (CREATE, READ, UPDATE, DELETE) with Japanese labels and English codes for internationalization support.

**Permission Management**: Sample permissions for audition and talent management with detailed descriptions, operation mappings, and display ordering.

**Role-Based Access Control**: Two role types implemented:
- **管理者 (Admin)**: Full system access with permissions [1,2,3,4,5]
- **ディレクター (Director)**: Limited access with permissions [1,2,4]

**API Endpoints**: The structure enables RESTful endpoints via my-json-server:
- `GET /api/permissions/operations` - Available operations
- `GET /api/permissions/list` - All permissions
- `GET /api/permissions/groups` - Permission groups
- `GET /api/roles/admin/detail` - Admin role details
- `GET /api/roles/director/detail` - Director role details

All JSON files are properly formatted and validated, providing a solid foundation for API testing and frontend development.

This PR enhances the existing Ezoic JavaScript integration with several improvements for better ad coverage, performance, and reliability across the BravoMail application.

## Changes Made

### 🚀 Performance Improvements
- **Added script preloading**: Implemented `<link rel="preload">` for Ezoic scripts (`sa.min.js` and `ezoic.js`) to improve loading performance
- **Enhanced initialization logic**: Added better timing and error handling for Ezoic script loading in production mode
- **Optimized ad slot definitions**: Improved automatic ad slot definition when Ezoic becomes available

### 📈 Expanded Ad Coverage
- **About page integration**: Added strategic header leaderboard ad placement to the About page
- **FAQ page integration**: Added main banner ad placement to the FAQ page for better monetization coverage
- **Maintained responsive design**: All new ad placements are fully responsive and properly styled

### 🔧 Configuration Enhancements
- **Updated site verification**: Changed meta tag from placeholder `bravomail-ezoic-verification` to more realistic format `ezoic-bravomail-email-verification-key`
- **Improved error handling**: Enhanced initialization function with better retry logic and graceful fallbacks
- **Better development experience**: Maintained clear ad placeholders in development mode with proper IDs

### 🎯 Technical Details

The integration now covers:
- **Homepage**: 3 strategic ad placements (header, main, footer)
- **About page**: 1 header leaderboard placement
- **FAQ page**: 1 main banner placement

All implementations follow Ezoic best practices:
- Privacy/consent script loads first (`sa.min.js`)
- Main Ezoic script loads second (`ezoic.js`)
- Proper async loading with performance optimizations
- Component-based React integration with lifecycle management
- Full TypeScript support with proper type definitions

### 📊 Testing Results

✅ All pages load correctly with ad placeholders in development mode  
✅ Build process completes successfully  
✅ Scripts load in correct order with proper error handling  
✅ Responsive design maintained across all device sizes  
✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality  

The Ezoic integration is now production-ready with enhanced coverage and performance optimizations while maintaining the existing high-quality codebase standards.

* Passing existing tests

feat: 为插件表面添加键盘焦点管理

1. 在 PluginSurface 类中添加 setKeyboardFocus 方法，通过 Wayland seat 处 理键盘焦点
2. 将方法暴露为 Q_INVOKABLE 以便 QML 访问
3. 在 ShellSurfaceItemProxy 中实现悬停时的焦点处理
4. 包含必要的 QWaylandSeat 头文件用于键盘焦点管理
5. 确保与插件表面交互时能正确处理键盘输入

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce keyboard focus management for plugin surfaces in the compositor and QML layer

New Features:
- Add setKeyboardFocus method to PluginSurface to assign keyboard focus via the Wayland seat
- Expose setKeyboardFocus as Q_INVOKABLE for QML access
- Invoke setKeyboardFocus in ShellSurfaceItemProxy on hover to enable keyboard input

Enhancements:
- Include QWaylandSeat header to support keyboard focus operations

> Closes #126

This pull request introduces several improvements to the `@layerfig/config` library and its documentation. The changes include consolidating imports for better readability, refactoring the codebase to align with updated module structures, enhancing test coverage, and reorganizing server-specific files for clarity. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Documentation Improvements:
* Consolidated imports in code examples across various documentation files (e.g., `getting-started/base-files.astro`, `guides/dynamic-environment.mdx`, `setup/sources.mdx`) to reduce redundancy and improve readability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8c91845dc3d1022068ddee0ef6706fdd321ac5b0b70350cbad3f2e2e478982ccL15-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b9e2f57cc0800068b6458dba8c92ed002c893b115f2d54fd5fe5a8f7652e8692L12-R12) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a8cc9c00fd3a6a4b1255df6e0ccfa80b3d378f9efbfc2f44243e5a092ce9c7a4L149-R152)
* Updated code snippets to reflect changes in import paths and meta information for better alignment with the new module structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f294f8180886e4ca03cceff4bbc20ddb92d0a72a97d5e6ab7081e87bf1c18965L60-R58) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4032954fb9127088049a1a9829641907a2600a19d703c169b9eeeaf47959bec4L52-R53)

### Codebase Refactoring:
* Refactored `ConfigBuilder` to support multiple source types (`ObjectSource` and `EnvironmentVariableSource`) and updated the `addSource` method to validate source types. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-62e233c525b6b83452055a3848b5d3b814e6829b2324b8e7288cf37a1ec9c51eR1-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-62e233c525b6b83452055a3848b5d3b814e6829b2324b8e7288cf37a1ec9c51eL37-R47)

* Added a new test case for `EnvironmentVariableSource` in `client.test.ts` to verify its functionality.

author: ash-5
body:
Summary:
Updated instantiations of stdClass to use the global namespace (\stdClass) to ensure compatibility and prevent conflicts when used within namespaced code.

Reason for Change:
In namespaced contexts, using new stdClass() without the leading backslash can cause PHP to look for stdClass within the current namespace, which may not exist. This can lead to runtime errors or unexpected behavior.

author: huitema
body:
Verify that a connection can be established and then closed using the UDP connect proxy.

This meant testing the "intercept" API (capture of outgoing packets from the client and passing them to the proxy connection),
and developing the "redirect" API (capture of incoming packets on the proxy and passing them to the client). Also, fixing the handling of packets too long to be passed over the proxy connection. And of course developing the initial test of
UDP connect.

UDP connect is still a work in progress: we need to handle the passing of the proxy address to the client in a way that conform with the UDP Connect RFC.

This commit resolves the `sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (sqlite3.OperationalError) no such table` error by:

1.  **Correcting `init_db.py`:** Removed the unnecessary `.replace()` call on the database URI to ensure the database file is created in the correct project root location.
2.  **Fixing Model Relationships:** Populated `app/models/__init__.py` with imports for all models. This resolves a circular dependency issue that prevented SQLAlchemy from correctly mapping relationships between tables (e.g., between `User` and `News`).
3.  **Refactoring Scripts:** Updated `create_superuser.py` to use the new centralized model imports.

These changes ensure that the database tables are created correctly upon initialization and that scripts interacting with the database models function as expected.

author: lordhookie
body:
## About The Pull Request

Severely throttles the damage output of some of the most drastically overperforming weapons on the station.
## How This Contributes To The Nova Sector Roleplay Experience

The MMRs are two frankly **ludicrous** weapons capable of easily outperforming weapons wielded by assops or even the dreaded pulse rifle, which functions as an ERT unit's diagetic way to smite people at behest of the admins. The 'marksman' rifle outputs huge bursts of damage that will nearly instantly down you, and only has a TTK above two seconds due to an obscene fire delay strapped to it. The automatic MMR, on the other hand, is through-and-through ridiculous, sporting a TTD of **1.3**. 

These weapons are overcentralizing and completely nullify anything you point them at. We have balance problems with guns, but these weapons personified them entirely; heretics can be mowed down and redsuits frankly stepped on by a weapon that barely costs more than the starting funds.

Replacement statistics are blunt, heavily penalizing their damage output (as they fire a round intended for semi-automatic rifles in fully automatic fire) to bring it more in line with other weapons on the server, with consideration given to their very large magazine capacities and versatility.

I will admit outright: I am not entirely happy with this solution, and I would rather move the MMRs entirely and place a more fitting weapon in their stead, but this solution requires sprites I at the moment do not have. I would _like_ to simply re-use our old sprites for this purpose, or use the sprites from our cousins in Bubber and Splurt, but I have received some pushback to the idea from staff; if I had permission to use them I could get it out quite soon, but without I'm going to have to request sprites from some people.

Their current performance without this change, **with a pulse rifle for reference:**


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc3a77bf-d615-4017-b144-0084da00b81a

(the rifle is fired at a slightly longer distance than the mmr)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16279af9-3bb4-4d52-b664-ee2f3c51e312

author: drpsyko101
body:
This PR aims to reduce hard-coded table conversion from native Unreal objects into Lua tables.

### New (kinda) endpoints!

* `GET /settings/traffic` - Get current AI traffic spawner settings
* `POST /settings/traffic` - Formerly at `/status/traffic`, now handles just AI traffic
* `POST /settings` - Handles setting the server configuration
* `PATCH /events/<guid>` - Formerly `POST /events/<guid>` for modifying event's name and race setup
* `POST /events/<guid>/players` - Add player(s) into an event
* `DELETE /events/<guid>/players` - Remove player(s) from an event
* `GET /houses/<guid>` - Get specific house based on the given GUID

### Breaking changes

* Most of the hard-coded table conversions have been removed in favour of the new C++ Lua table parser. This should be less prone to human error during parsing and may increase performance in certain scenarios. However, structs are not yet supported.
* `FTransform` to JSON output now uses `Translation` instead of `Location` as one of its keys.

### Bugfixes

* Fix possible truncate error when passing `FGuid` as a string.
* Fix the event's lap amount not updated on creation or during edits
* Fix event setup not properly set on creation/edit
* Fix garage spawner giving wrong output and not doing anything
* Fix #50 by relegating the pinned announcement to any available admin player

Fixes #DXP-492

# What

<!-- Describe the changes you made. -->

- Refactored the `get_transaction_receipt` function in `backend/protocol_rpc/endpoints.py` to improve code readability and handle potential `None` values for `to_address` and `from_address`.
- Introduced local variables `to_addr` and `from_addr` to store `to_address` and `from_address` respectively, reducing repeated calls to `transaction.get`.

# Why

author: dbggr
body:
## Task 2: Database Setup and Schema Implementation

This PR implements the complete database setup and schema for the Network Source of Truth system.

### Changes Made

#### Database Connection & Configuration
- **`api/database/connection.ts`**: SQLite database connection with proper configuration
  - WAL journal mode for better concurrency
  - Foreign key constraints enabled
  - Graceful shutdown handling
  - Environment-based database path configuration

#### Database Schema
- **`api/database/schema.sql`**: Complete database schema
  - `groups` table for organizing network services
  - `network_services` table with foreign key relationships
  - Indexes for performance optimization
  - Triggers for automatic timestamp updates

#### Migration System
- **`api/database/index.ts`**: Full migration management system
  - Version tracking with migrations table
  - Automatic migration execution
  - Transaction-safe migration application
  - Default data seeding functionality

#### Database Utilities
- **`api/utils/database.ts`**: Query execution helpers
  - Standardized query result interface
  - Transaction support
  - JSON field serialization utilities
  - Proper error handling integration

#### Error Handling
- **`api/utils/errors.ts`**: Custom error classes
  - Database-specific error types
  - Constraint violation detection
  - Standardized error handling

#### Scripts & Tools
- **`scripts/init-db.ts`**: Database initialization script
- **`scripts/seed-db.ts`**: Default data seeding script  
- **`scripts/test-db.ts`**: Database functionality testing
- **`scripts/tsconfig.json`**: TypeScript configuration for scripts

#### Package Configuration
- Added `ts-node` dependency for TypeScript script execution
- Updated npm scripts for database operations:
  - `npm run db:init` - Initialize database
  - `npm run db:seed` - Seed default data
  - `npm run db:test` - Test database functionality

### Requirements Addressed
- **6.1**: Database driver installation and configuration ✅
- **6.2**: Database initialization with proper schema ✅  
- **6.3**: Migration system for schema updates ✅

### Testing
All functionality has been tested and verified:
- Database initialization works correctly
- Migration system applies migrations properly
- Default groups are seeded successfully
- Error handling works as expected
- All npm scripts execute without errors

### Database Schema Details
- **Groups**: `id`, `name`, `description`, timestamps
- **Network Services**: `id`, `group_id`, `name`, `domain`, `internal_ports`, `external_ports`, `vlan`, `cidr`, `ip_address`, `tags`, timestamps
- **Migrations**: Version tracking for schema updates

The database is now ready for the next implementation phase (data models and validation).

author: wallyworld
body:
The allowed size for secret content was too restrictive for some types of secret content, eg CA certs.
k8s allows a max size of 1MiB, so we will do that in Juju as well.

Previously the max individual value size was 8KiB ad the overall content size was 64KiB. We'll just make both 1MiB.
Note that the maximum content size is the base64 encoded size, so the actual allowed non-encoded content size is approx 3/4 of that.

## QA steps

On both k8s and lxd, bootstrap and add a model.

```
echo "key: $(cat /dev/zero | tr '\0' A | head -c 786430)" > out.txt
juju add-secret test --file out.txt
juju show secret test --reveal
```

## Links

author: birojulia
body:
## What's Added

- Implemented `Dashboard.vue` view
- Added a basic `SearchBar` component (manual search via button)
- Integrated Inertia route with search query param
- Display search results if input is given, or fallback to dashboard content

## How It Works

- The search bar uses Vue `emits` to notify the parent component when a search is triggered.
- If the user enters a query and hits the search button, a GET request is made to `/dashboard?search=...`
- The backend uses IGDBService to search games or fallback to latest/popular games
- Results appear only if `hasSearched` is `true`, otherwise default sections are shown

## UI

- Responsive cards for game results
- Two sections: New Releases & Popular Games when no search is active

## Notes

- Search is **manual**, not live (no debounce or autosubmit)
- Next step: improve UX (error handling, debounce etc.)

author: aadishv
body:
The `getLists` query was previously fetching all lists along with all of their associated items (nodes) on every request. This was highly inefficient and resulted in significant bandwidth consumption, estimated at ~800MB per week, due to the frequency of the query.

This commit refactors the data fetching logic: - The `getLists` query in `convex/lists.ts` has been modified to only return the lists, without their nested items. - The `getItems` query is now used in `AuthenticatedApp.tsx` to fetch items only for the currently selected list, triggered when the selection changes. - The frontend component was updated to merge the list and item data on the client side.

This change dramatically reduces the amount of data transferred on initial load and subsequent refreshes, leading to an estimated 95%+ reduction in bandwidth for this feature and a more responsive user experience.

author: louis-cqrl
body:
### What does this PR do?

This PR introduces a new set of built-in **gRPC telemetry metrics** for the Datadog Agent.

Specifically:
- Adds server and client-side gRPC interceptors that emit telemetry.
- Provides metrics for request counts, errors, latencies, payload sizes, and active requests.
- Adds utility wrappers in `pkg/util/grpc` to simplify interceptor setup.
- Updates all internal gRPC server instantiations to use the new unified metrics-aware interceptors.
- Introduces `ServerOptionsWithMetricsAndAuth` and related helper functions to combine metrics and authentication logic safely.
- Adds new telemetry definitions in `metrics.go` and logic for collecting them in `interceptors.go`.

The following metrics are now available:
| Metric Name                     | Type      | Description                                     |
| ------------------------------ | --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `grpc.request_count`           | Counter   | Total number of gRPC requests processed         |
| `grpc.error_count`             | Counter   | Total number of gRPC errors encountered         |
| `grpc.request_duration_seconds`| Histogram | Distribution of gRPC request latencies          |
| `grpc.payload_size_bytes`      | Histogram | Distribution of payload sizes for gRPC calls    |


### Motivation

- Improve visibility into internal gRPC communications across Agent components.
- Enable better performance monitoring and debugging of gRPC-based data paths.
- Lay the groundwork for future enhancements like dynamic latency analysis, error tracking, or profiling by exposing low-level RPC metrics.
- Standardize interceptor setup across the codebase, reducing risk of misconfiguration.


### Describe how you validated your changes

- **Unit Tests**: Added coverage for the new interceptors.
- **Manual Validation**:
  - Started various Agent components locally with interceptors enabled.
  - Observed telemetry output from active gRPC streams (via logs and metrics sink).
- **Regression Coverage**: Ensured no breaking changes to existing gRPC auth or TLS configuration logic.


### Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs

- **Telemetry Overhead**: Introducing metrics collection may introduce slight CPU/memory cost. However, metrics are batched and histogram buckets are optimized for typical gRPC call durations and sizes.

### Additional Notes

- The new `pkg/util/grpc` package is designed to be used consistently across components; this will help future initiatives such as unified observability.
- No behavior is changed in existing gRPC endpoints besides the added telemetry.
- This PR is part of ongoing efforts to improve internal instrumentation under the `COAT` initiative.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Users experienced a connection error when running the Agent executable:

```
Inventory Management System - Agent
===================================
API Base URL: http://localhost:5093
...
HTTP Error: Hedef makine etkin olarak reddettiğinden bağlantı kurulamadı. (localhost:5093)
Device data stored offline due to network error.
```

The issue occurred because the Agent tried to connect to the API at startup, but the API service wasn't running. Users needed both components to start automatically when Windows boots and run continuously in the background.

## Solution

This PR implements comprehensive Windows Service support for both the API and Agent components, enabling automatic startup and background operation.

### Key Features

- **Automatic Startup**: Both API and Agent services start automatically when Windows boots
- **Dependency Management**: Agent service waits for API service to start first (delayed auto-start)
- **Background Operation**: Services run silently without user interaction
- **Event Logging**: Full integration with Windows Event Viewer for monitoring
- **Dual Mode Support**: Agent supports both console mode (for testing) and service mode

### Installation

Simple one-command installation as Administrator:

```powershell
.\scripts\Install-WindowsServices.ps1
```

### Service Configuration

- **API Service**: `InventoryManagementApi` - Automatic startup
- **Agent Service**: `InventoryManagementAgent` - Delayed automatic startup with API dependency
- **Security**: Both services run under LocalSystem account
- **Networking**: Firewall rule automatically configured for port 5093
- **Storage**: Environment variables configured for offline data storage

### Management Tools

- PowerShell installer and uninstaller scripts
- Batch file utilities for service management
- Integration with Windows Services management console (`services.msc`)
- Comprehensive documentation and troubleshooting guides

### Technical Implementation

- Added `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.WindowsServices` package to both projects
- Created `InventoryAgentService` background service class for periodic inventory scanning
- Modified `Program.cs` files to support both console and service modes
- Implemented proper service lifecycle management with graceful shutdown
- Added Windows Event Log provider for service logging

### Testing Verified

- Build process successful with no breaking changes
- Console mode functionality preserved and working
- Service mode tested and confirmed working
- API-Agent communication verified
- Service dependency management confirmed
- Installation and uninstallation scripts validated

## Result

The connection error is permanently resolved. Users can now install the system once, and both API and Agent will automatically start every time Windows boots, ensuring continuous inventory monitoring without manual intervention.

## Files Added/Modified

- **Service Support**: Enhanced `Inventory.Api` and `Inventory.Agent.Windows` projects
- **Installation Scripts**: PowerShell and batch installers/uninstallers  
- **Management Tools**: Service management utilities
- **Documentation**: Quick start guide and comprehensive setup documentation
- **Project Files**: Added Windows Service package references

This solution provides enterprise-grade deployment capabilities while maintaining backward compatibility with existing console-based usage.

author: crlees
body:
# 🎨 updateUser 폼 스타일링 및 정렬 개선

## 📖 변경사항 요약
사용자 정보 수정 페이지(`updateUser.xml`)의 폼 요소들에 대한 종합적인 UI/UX 개선을 진행했습니다.

## 🔧 주요 개선사항

### 1. **시각적 일관성 향상**
- 모든 폼 요소의 `border-radius`를 **4px로 통일**
- 입력 필드, 선택박스, 버튼, 컨테이너 등 전체 요소 적용

### 2. **WebSquare Select 컴포넌트 정렬 개선**
- 경력, 직무분야, 희망연봉 선택박스의 **텍스트 수직 정렬 문제 해결**
- CSS `display: flex`, `align-items: center` 적용
- 내부 table 및 document 요소 정렬 최적화

### 3. **선호지역 섹션 레이아웃 개선**
- 선택된 지역 태그와 지역 선택 버튼 사이에 **15px 여백 추가**
- 더욱 깔끔하고 여유 있는 레이아웃 구현

## 🎯 개선 효과
- ✅ 전체 폼의 시각적 일관성 확보
- ✅ 사용자 인터페이스 가독성 향상
- ✅ 모던하고 세련된 디자인 완성
- ✅ 사용자 경험(UX) 개선

## 🖼️ 변경된 요소들
- `.form-input` - 텍스트 입력 필드
- `.form-textarea` - 텍스트영역
- `.form-select` - 선택박스 + 정렬 개선
- `.btn` - 버튼들
- `.location-container` - 지역 선택 컨테이너
- `.location-option` - 지역 선택 버튼
- `.location-tag-container` - 선택된 태그 여백

## 🧪 테스트 완료
- 브라우저 테스트를 통해 모든 변경사항 검증 완료
- 반응형 레이아웃 정상 작동 확인

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Style**
  * 여러 UI 요소(입력 필드, 텍스트영역, 선택박스, 버튼 등)의 모서리 둥글기(border-radius)가 4px로 변경되어 덜 둥글게 보입니다.
  * 선택박스(.form-select)와 내부 요소의 텍스트가 수직 중앙 정렬되도록 스타일이 개선되었습니다.
  * 위치 태그 컨테이너(.location-tag-container)에 하단 여백이 추가되어 선택된 태그와 버튼 사이 간격이 넓어졌습니다.

The build-helm-chart task relied on the images in the chart to be updated prior for the chart running, requiring that the update of the image that the charts deploys and the chart itself are not changed at part of the same commit.

This change introduces version 0.2 in which the image and chart are expected to be built at the same time, for which the task for building the chart needs to substitute the images within the chart with values per what is being built at the same time.

## 📌 작업 개요

<!-- 어떤 기능/버그를 작업했는지 간단히 설명해주세요 -->

### 1. 환불 기능 구현
- `/mypage/refund` 페이지에서 현금 환불 기능 추가
- POST `/api/payments/refund` API 연동
- 환불 성공 시 공통 완료 모달 (`CashSuccessModal`) 표시
### 2. 캐시 충전/환불 공통 컴포넌트 리팩토링!
- `ChargeCashContent.tsx` → `CashActionContent.tsx`로 통합
   - `mode` prop (`"charge"` | `"refund"`) 기반 동작 분기
   - 금액 선택, 버튼, 카드 컴포넌트 재사용
- 완료 모달도 `CashSuccessModal` 하나로 통합
   - `mode` 값에 따라 "충전되었습니다" / "환불되었습니다" UI 분기 처리
- zustand 모달 store도 `useCashSuccessModalStore` 하나로 통합

1. **충전 흐름**
   1. 사용자가 금액을 선택하고 `결제하기` 버튼 클릭
   2. `TossPaymentModal`이 열리고 Toss 위젯 렌더링됨
   3. Toss에서 결제 성공 → `successUrl` (`/mypage/charge/success`)로 리디렉션됨
   4. `useHandleTossSuccess()`에서 Toss 응답 정보 검증 및 결제 승인 요청
   5. 검증 성공 → `/mypage?payment=success`로 이동
   6. `MyPageContent`에서 `payment=success` 감지 → `CashSuccessModal` 열림
   7. 완료 버튼 누르면 `/mypage`로 이동하고 캐시 초기화

2. **환불 흐름**
   1. 사용자가 환불 금액 선택 후 `현금으로 전환하기` 클릭
   2. `requestRefund` API 호출 → 환불 처리
   3. 환불 성공 시 `CashSuccessModal` 열림
   4. 완료 버튼 누르면 `/mypage`로 이동하고 캐시 초기화
### 3. 캐시 충전 결제중 success page UI 구현

body:
feat(okurite): implement comprehensive success rate dashboard with visual analytics

This commit adds the statistics view that completes our success rate tracking implementation, directly addressing the client's requirement to "improve the posting success rate to over 60% and make the confirmation visible in the UI."

## Key Features Implemented

1. **Real-time Submission Metrics Dashboard**
   - Displays total attempts, successful submissions, and pending submissions in a responsive grid layout
   - Calculates and prominently displays success rate percentage with visual indicators (✅/⚠️)
   - Color-codes success rate (green ≥60%, red <60%) to immediately highlight performance status

2. **Failure Analysis Visualization**
   - Implements a visual bar chart showing failure distribution by type
   - Calculates and displays percentage breakdown of failure reasons
   - Provides actionable data for diagnosing submission issues

3. **Responsive UI Design**
   - Mobile-friendly grid layout using CSS Grid
   - Clean, professional styling embedded directly in the view
   - Intuitive color coding and visual hierarchy for quick data comprehension

4. **Action-Oriented Interface**
   - Includes "改善アクション" button when success rate is below target
   - Clear navigation with "戻る" button to return to main interface
   - Visual feedback that enables quick identification of problem areas

## Technical Implementation Notes

- Fully integrated with the existing statistics controller action
- Uses inline CSS for immediate deployment without asset pipeline changes
- Implements responsive design principles for all device sizes
- Calculates percentages dynamically on the server side for accuracy
- Handles edge cases (zero submissions, no failures) gracefully

This dashboard provides the client with the visibility needed to monitor and improve their submission success rate, fulfilling the critical requirement to "accurately determine and record whether each submission was successful or not" while making performance data immediately actionable.

The implementation follows Rails best practices for view templates while delivering a professional, production-ready analytics interface that meets the client's 60% success rate target monitoring needs.

### 1. `app.js`
#### 🧩 SAST Analysis Summary
| Line | Type | Level | CWE | Ref |
|----|----|-----|---|---|
| 168~176 | Cryptographic Issues | ⚠️ WARNING | CWE-522 | [🔗](https://owasp.org/Top10/A04_2021-Insecure_Design) |
